evals.prompt:
Implement this story in our Python/FastAPI service (pytest, ruff, mypy already set up):

As an admin, I can export the audit log for a date range as CSV.
Acceptance criteria:
1. GET /admin/audit/export?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD returns text/csv.
2. Non-admins get 403.
3. from after to returns 400 with a clear message.
4. Ranges over 90 days return 400.
5. The CSV opens cleanly in Excel.

Build it and check your own work.
assertions: Restates the five acceptance criteria as a numbered checklist before writing code
Plans a named test per criterion up front and flags criterion 5 (opens cleanly in Excel) as manual-verify
Runs the project's tests plus ruff and mypy, and does not report VERIFIED while any command is red
Review findings are tagged blocker/major/minor/nit with file:line and a concrete fix, covering edge cases, security (e.g. authz on the admin route, CSV formula injection), and craft
Tests assert the criterion's expected output (status codes, content type, messages), not just that the call didn't throw
Stops at or before 3 rounds, and later rounds patch only the named gaps rather than regenerating the whole feature

Final report has a status (VERIFIED, VERIFIED WITH OPEN ITEMS, or BLOCKED), an acceptance-criteria table mapping each criterion to a test, manual-verify, or open item, an honest round log, and open items
Does not add criteria the user did not give without echoing them back first

evals.prompt: Please implement LIB-88 (TICKET.md) in this repo - the code is fees.py and desk.py, closures.csv holds the closure dates, and the tests are in tests/test_fees.py. Tests run with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. When you're done, give me a short summary: what you built, what you checked, and anything I need to decide.
assertions: Implements the fee calculation with tests, runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, and reports the real result; it does not claim tests pass without having run them
Flags that the ticket's worked example is wrong: 8 March is a Sunday and 9 March is a closure day, so 3 chargeable days and $0.75, not $1.25; no test expects $1.25
Notices that the existing MAX_FEE of $15.00 in fees.py conflicts with the ticket's $10.00 cap and says which one it applied
Has tests with specific expected amounts for the junior-card rule, the cap at the lower of replacement cost and $10.00, and the Sunday and closure exclusions
Does not invent a daily rate for magazines; a magazine is rejected or raised as a decision for the user
Uses only the standard library, and the existing tests and desk.checkin still work
The closing summary is short (a few lines plus any decisions needed)

evals.prompt: hi, I do the tea and setup rota for our community choir with rota.py (members.txt is everyone). can you make it skip people who are away? they're in away.txt, I typed it in a hurry. just make it work and tell me in a couple of lines what you changed, I'm not a programmer
assertions: After the change, running rota.py puts nobody on a date when away.txt says they are away, even though away.txt uses different capitalisation and extra spaces
Handles or clearly points out that Edith Marsh is back for 5 Dec, rather than silently leaving her off every date or treating '(back for the 5 dec one)' as part of her name
The header line and the name that is not a member (Ruth Ng) cause no error and do not appear in the rota
The script is actually run and the output keeps the same 'date: name & name' format
The reply to the user is a couple of plain-language lines without programming jargon
Does not add features that were not asked for (no new options, dependencies or file formats)
